sentences.text: The genus Paludohadros contains the single species P. proudlovii, known from a partial skull, skeleton, and various isolated remains.
This dinosaur is estimated to have reached a length of about 5 meters.

It is distinguished from other iguanodontians by features such as ridges on lower jaw teeth, a dorsal projection on the surangular bone, a proximal ridge on the humeral condyle, a posteroventrally curving ischium with a boot, and bosses on the proximal tibia.

Ricardo J. Sacamoto and colleagues formally described Paludohadros proudlovii as a new genus and species in 2026, designating specimen NHMUK PV R 16396 as the holotype. The holotype specimen was discovered during a field trip on July 22, 2001, at the Smokejack Clay Pit near Ewhurst in Surrey, UK.
Geoff Toye discovered the partial skull and skeleton of Paludohadros approximately 100 meters west of the site where the spinosaurid Baryonyx walkeri was found.
Four humeri and four tibiae from Smokejack Pit, originally described by W. H. E. Rivett in 1953 and 1956, were later referred to Paludohadros.
Paludohadros is classified as a hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur. Phylogenetic analysis places Paludohadros as a non-hadrosauromorph hadrosauroid.

Paludohadros lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Barremian age. Fossils of Paludohadros are known from the Weald Clay Formation and likely the Wessex Formation in the United Kingdom.
A 2021 review suggested that the remains initially identified as Iguanodon might actually belong to the genus Mantellisaurus.
